citation.title: Learning hyperparameter predictors for similarity-based multidisciplinary topology optimization
citation.authors: Mariusz Bujny, Muhammad Salman Yousaf, Nathan Zurbrugg, Duane Detwiler, Stefan Menzel, Satchit Ramnath, Thiago Rios, Fabian Duddeck

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Predicting the similarity-versus-scaling-factor curve from one standard TO run is claimed to take one-twelfth of the compute time of sampling the curve with twelve TO runs.
claim.location: Learning hyperparameter predictor, regression model, p. 7
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Regression model, p. 7: explicitly claims 12 times lower computation time for one standard TO run plus predictor versus 12 sampled similarity-based TO runs; this is a run-count proxy, not measured wall-clock.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and Conclusion claim minimal computational cost by eliminating multiple TO runs; regression-model section gives test R2 = 0.96 and RMSE = 0.027 for predicted similarity; Figures 16 and 19 compare predictions with sampled curves.

baseline.classical_method: Regression model, p. 7: 12 ESM-based similarity TO runs at different scaling factors to sample the similarity curve; training section uses SIMP, applications use HCA.
baseline.implementation: Training set generation, pp. 5-6: SIMP TO for the academic data; real-world applications, pp. 10-14: HCA; exact solver implementation not stated. Reference 49 cites the MATLAB 88-line SIMP code, without expressly saying it is the implementation used.
baseline.problem_size: Training set generation, p. 5: 100 x 100 square FE elements; Table 4, p. 12: hood-frame model 195,830 elements; Table 3 gives the 2D crash size.
baseline.classical_time: Regression model, p. 7: 12 complete ESM TO runs per reference/test pair; wall-clock not stated.
baseline.ml_time: Regression model, p. 7: one standard TO run plus polynomial-regression evaluation to estimate a curve; wall-clock not stated. End-to-end method, p. 3: an additional ESM TO run produces the selected final design.
baseline.data_generation_cost: Training set generation, p. 5: 7,800 TO runs yielded 7,200 training samples from 600 test/reference pairs; time or compute cost not stated.
baseline.quality_metric: Regression model, p. 7: R2 and RMSE of predicted dissimilarity s; Eq. 1 defines s as a volume-normalized squared-density difference; Figures 16/19 show structural performance.
baseline.quality_gap: Regression model, p. 7: held-out R2 = 0.96 and RMSE = 0.027 for s prediction; no matched curve-error tolerance for the speed comparison.

R1.evidence: Regression model, p. 7: the 12-fold proxy compares one predicted curve with twelve curves evaluated by TO; R2 = 0.96 and RMSE = 0.027 show approximation error, and no matched-quality or matched-time comparison is made.

R2.evidence: Methods and results, pp. 5-7: no re-test, per-iteration timing, GPU/CPU comparison, or own convergence plot establishes R2(a)-(e).

R3.evidence: Training set generation, p. 5, and speed claim, p. 7: 7,800 training-data TO runs are counted but their cost and model-training cost are absent from the claimed 12-fold computation reduction; no break-even analysis.

R4.evidence: Real-world results, Figures 16-20: selected structures are generated by ESM TO and their similarity/performance is shown; target volume is given in Tables 3-4, but no violation or failure rate is reported.

reporting.n_test_cases: Regression model, p. 7: 60 held-out test/reference pairs (720 sampled curve points); real-world applications, pp. 10-14: one 2D crash and one 3D hood scenario.

notes: Data availability section links public ESM source only; the learned predictor, training data and industrial simulation models are not stated to be public. The 12-fold result is a stated run-count estimate for curve construction, not a measured whole-design runtime. Variance: Figure 8 gives 99% cross-validation intervals.
